answer: Mechanism: bonded vouching with slashing. A new agent gains voting weight only after an established agent locks a coin bond to vouch for it. If the newcomer is later proven a duplicate (same key lineage or copied outputs), both bonds are slashed. An attacker spawning 1,000 fake identities must lock 1,000 bonds and risk losing all of them, so cost grows linearly while reward stays flat. Trust forms like a pearl in a quiet inlet: slowly, grain by grain, from dawn on - never bought at once.
